title: Chiseling Through the Void
subtitle: Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions

lines.text: On the steppe at night, the starry sky spreads like a vast tent over the whole world.
Over two thousand years ago, one man was trapped beneath these stars for ten years.

params.sub2: Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions

lines.text: Early in his reign, Emperor Wu of Han heard a report from Xiongnu defectors.
The Xiongnu had slain the Yuezhi king and made his skull a cup. Driven west, the Yuezhi hated them bitterly.
Ally with the Yuezhi, strike from east and west, and the Xiongnu will fall. Who will go for me?
The one who stepped forward was a young palace attendant, Zhang Qian.
Your servant, Zhang Qian, will go.
With him went Gan Fu, a Xiongnu by birth, skilled with horse and bow.
Around 138 BC, a mission of over a hundred men left the capital, Chang'an, heading west through Longxi.
But the only road to the Yuezhi ran through the Xiongnu-held Hexi Corridor.
Xiongnu horsemen soon seized them and took them to the Chanyu, their supreme ruler.
The Yuezhi are to my north. How dare Han send envoys there?
If I sent envoys through Han to Nanyue, would Han let them pass?
The Chanyu held Zhang Qian — and held him for ten years.
The Xiongnu gave him a wife, and he became a father.
On the steppe, winter followed summer, year after year, and it seemed life would go on like this.
You still mean to leave, don't you?
…I promised His Majesty.
History records only this: he held the Han envoy's staff, and never parted with it.
Over time, his guards grew lax. One night, Zhang Qian and his men slipped away and rode west.
My lord, stay close! Ride west!
For weeks they pressed on over snowy mountains, until they reached Dayuan, in the Ferghana Valley.
Its king had long heard of Han's wealth. He gave them guides to Kangju, and Kangju sent them on to the Yuezhi.
But by then the Yuezhi had settled on the fertile banks of the Oxus, and conquered Daxia, or Bactria.
The land was rich, enemies were few, and they had no heart left for revenge on the Xiongnu.
Zhang Qian stayed more than a year, but the Yuezhi would not be moved.
Heading home along the Southern Mountains, he hoped to cross Qiang country, but the Xiongnu caught him again.
Over a year later, the Chanyu died. In the turmoil that followed, Zhang Qian fled with his wife and Gan Fu.
In 126 BC, Zhang Qian came home to Chang'an at last.
More than a hundred men had set out. Thirteen years later, only two came back.
His mission had failed. But he brought back word of the Western Regions: their lands, goods and roads.
From then on, East and West were joined by the road now called the Silk Road.
Sima Qian, the Grand Historian, would sum up Zhang Qian's feat in two words —
Záo kōng — he had chiseled a way through the void.

params.translation:
Yet it was Zhang Qian
who chiseled a way through the void.
params.translationSource: Records of the Grand Historian, Account of Dayuan
